feed.description: Conversaciones sobre construcción de senderos: drenaje, trazado, y las personas que construyen la ruta. Contraparte en español de Singletrack Sessions.
feed.title: Sesiones de Sendero

bullets: Drainage is the highest-leverage design decision on any trail; ignoring it means rebuilding the trail from scratch a year later.
The most common mistake new builders make is digging too steep a grade — once that lands, the rest of the design decisions get easier.
Bench cuts on sidehills are not optional: the shortcut on day one becomes the washout in year three.
Soil structure matters more than people assume, a pattern that held across three separate crews.
Land-stewardship conversations belong before the first dig, because the framing exposes which trade-offs a project is making.
Machine-built versus hand-built trail is a position Javier Benavides has revised rather than held from the outset.
summary.raw_text: Drainage is the highest-leverage design decision on any trail — ignore it and the trail gets rebuilt from scratch a year later. Javier Benavides walks through the grade mistakes new builders make, why bench cuts on sidehills are not optional, and why land-stewardship conversations have to happen before the first dig.
summary.title: Drainage First: Building Trails That Last
